data.hypothesis: Correct two-target-per-thread trials at 96 and 128 threads measured 0.002554 s and 0.002585 s, respectively, both slower than the 0.001844 s baseline; three- and four-target trials at 128 threads were slower still. Test a five-warp, 160-thread block while keeping two targets per thread and source-register reuse fixed. The intermediate 320-target group may trade fewer CTAs against block scheduling and occupancy; no speedup is assumed.

memory_lessons.applicability: A block-size comparison can test CTA geometry while holding the two-target register-coarsening factor constant.
memory_lessons.claim: Observed valid trials measured 0.002554 s for two targets per thread at 96 threads, 0.002585 s at 128 threads, 0.003349 s for three targets per thread at 128 threads, and 0.004165 s for four targets per thread at 128 threads. These trials do not establish why the variants differed.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: If the 160-thread candidate passes correctness, compare its official measurements with the valid 96- and 128-thread two-target trials.

data.notes: Only src/launch.json changes. The existing kernel maps first = blockIdx.x*(2*blockDim.x)+threadIdx.x and second = first+blockDim.x, independently guards both targets, and reuses each source load across the two accumulations. With block=160, items_per_block=320 matches that mapping; shared memory remains unused. The controller should perform full correctness checks before measuring all scored sizes. No result is claimed for this candidate.
transformations: Set block=160 and items_per_block=320, with shared_memory_bytes=0.
Retain the kernel's explicit two-target mapping: each thread covers target offsets threadIdx.x and blockDim.x within a 320-target block group.
Retain independent tail guards and writes for each target, reusing each loaded source value across both target accumulations.
